groups.title: Soft capsule (D60400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: There is a daytime product and a night-time product. For the daytime product, adults and people aged 15 years and over take 2 capsules at a time, 2 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. For the night-time product, adults and people aged 15 years and over take 2 capsules at a time, once a day, 30 minutes after a meal.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure (daytime product); or if you are breast-feeding (night-time product).

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis related to pseudoephedrine (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occur; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery (night-time product). If you are breast-feeding, either do not take this medicine or stop breast-feeding (night-time product). If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with oral medicines that contain an antitussive (cough suppressant), an expectorant (phlegm medicine), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines), or with preparations containing diphenhydramine (including preparations applied to the skin) (night-time product). Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are being given medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids or the like. If you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

groups.title: Tablet (B05000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and to relieve the loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that go with constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time, once a day at bedtime. For the first dose, however, use the smallest amount, then increase or reduce it a little at a time while watching the form and condition of the stools.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal condition (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel).

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have severe abdominal pain or nausea and vomiting; if you have had rectal bleeding or bowel failure; or if the user is a child aged 10 years or under.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Do not chew the tablet.

Do not take this medicine together with antacids. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash and redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (C95300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin A, vitamin D, vitamin E, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B6 and vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during the growing years and in old age; to relieve dryness of the eyes; and for night blindness (poor vision at night), poor development of the bones and teeth, and the prevention of rickets.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 8 years and over: take 2 tablets at a time. Ages 36 months to under 8 years: take 1 tablet at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day. After a meal, let the tablet dissolve in the mouth or chew it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis or kidney disease; if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have kidney stones or severe kidney failure; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the child gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein; if you have gout or have had kidney stones; if you are short of folic acid; or if you have a tendency to thrombosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied in sufficient amounts by a normal diet, so do not let the supplementary dose exceed 5,000 IU a day. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are taking cardiac glycosides, oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful swollen joints, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness of the skin, loose stools, low blood pressure, facial flushing, an irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, cardiac arrest or reduced central nervous system function appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil, soy or peanuts or have had a reaction to them; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have severe kidney failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excess oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired cardiac or circulatory function, kidney impairment or low blood protein; if you have gout or kidney stones; if you are short of folic acid; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis; or if you are at particular risk from fat overload.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, levodopa, intravenous lipid preparations, oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. groups.title: Soft capsule (E36500ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or have had a reaction to it; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if the user is an older person, is debilitated or has a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or have ulcer or bleeding problems; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it continuously over a long period. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive (cough suppressant), an expectorant (phlegm medicine), another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. If you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes), cough with shortness of breath, difficulty breathing and fever, or symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) appear, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (D66000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supplement the vitamins, minerals and trace elements that are needed in greater amounts before, around and during pregnancy, to help prevent neural tube defects in the foetus, and to help prevent iron deficiency anaemia and folate deficiency anaemia during pregnancy.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet once a day with breakfast, or as directed by a doctor. If you have morning sickness, it is recommended that you take it at midday or in the evening. To help prevent neural tube defects in the foetus, take this medicine from at least 1 month before you plan to become pregnant. If you have not become pregnant after 2 to 3 months, the dose may be halved, so that you take 1/2 tablet once a day or 1 tablet once every 2 days.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are taking another medicine that contains vitamin A or vitamin D; if you have vitamin A excess or vitamin D excess; if you have kidney impairment or impaired iron utilisation; if you have high blood calcium or high calcium in the urine; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Taking 10,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day during pregnancy may increase the risk of birth defects, so if you may be pregnant or are in the first trimester of pregnancy, do not let the daily dose of vitamin A exceed 10,000 IU.

The stools may turn black and the urine may turn yellow, but this has no clinical significance.

If you have to take tetracyclines, leave an interval of 2 hours between them and this medicine. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are taking antiepileptics or anticonvulsants (for example carbamazepine, phenytoin, primidone and barbiturates) or another medicine containing vitamin A or vitamin D. Eating liver, liver products, cheese, eggs and the like while taking this medicine may take you over the daily requirement for vitamin A.

Discoloration of the stools may occur, and uncommonly headache, nausea, constipation, stomach discomfort, indigestion, vomiting, diarrhoea or reversible discoloration of the teeth; rarely the urine may turn yellow or dark; and very rarely allergy, an anaphylactic reaction, hives and asthma, itching, rash, a local skin reaction or an excessive irritation reaction may occur.

groups.usage: To prevent motion sickness, adults (aged 15 years and over) take 2 capsules at a time and children (aged 8 years to under 15 years) take 1 capsule at a time, 30 minutes before boarding. groups.caution:

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have had an allergic reaction (rash, reddening of the skin, itching and the like); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a heart disorder; if you are frail; if the user is an older person; or if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take this medicine together with other anti-emetics, cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, antihistamines, sedatives, antitussives and expectorants, or gastrointestinal analgesics and antispasmodics.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, headache, facial flushing, sensitivity to light, difficulty passing urine, thirst, constipation or diarrhoea appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye whenever needed.
groups.caution:
If eye pain, a change in vision, or persistent redness or irritation appears, stop using this medicine and consult a doctor.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if the user is a child aged 6 years or under.

If eye pain, a change in vision, or persistent redness or irritation appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
